newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian cabinet to meet Friday, justice on agenda.
newsitem.headline: Italian cabinet to meet Friday, justice on agenda.

text.p: The Italian cabinet will meet on Friday at 0730 GMT and will consider a packet of measures to reform the justice system, the government said in a statement.
The measures, proposed by Justice Minister Giovanni Maria Flick, would allow defendants facing jail terms of up to three years to negotiate their sentences provided they admitted guilt.
Flick urgently wants to overhaul Italy's creaking and tortuously slow justice system.

He has also proposed allowing the payment of negotiable damages in return for up to a third off the sentence and the application of fast-track procedures to some crimes punishable by life in jail, in which the maximum term would be 30 years.
Once approved by the cabinet, the package of measures will go before parliament for debate.
